name: When Should Kitchen Appliances Be Ordered During a Remodel?

mainEntity.name: Should I buy kitchen appliances before cabinet design or wait until the renovation is underway?
mainEntity.text: Should I buy kitchen appliances before cabinet design or wait until the renovation is underway?

acceptedAnswer.text: Appliances should be chosen early enough for the designer and trades to work from exact specifications. A refrigerator’s depth and door swing, a range’s power or gas needs, a dishwasher opening, a wall oven’s cutout, and a hood’s duct requirements can all change cabinet dimensions and utility locations. Provide the contractor with manufacturer installation sheets, not only product names or online dimensions. Confirm whether handles, doors, panels, ventilation, water lines, drain loops, shutoffs, and dedicated circuits require additional clearance. Ask who receives, stores, inspects, installs, and removes packaging. Do not assume a replacement model will fit if the selected appliance is delayed. Order long-lead items early, but coordinate delivery with secure storage and site readiness. Inspect for damage before installation and document serial numbers. The contract should state who pays for cabinet modifications caused by owner substitutions, incorrect specifications, delivery damage, or discontinued products. Finalize appliance choices before cabinet fabrication and rough-in work to reduce expensive changes.
acceptedAnswer.description: Select appliance models before final cabinet drawings and rough electrical or plumbing work. Exact dimensions, door swings, ventilation, power requirements, water connections, and installation clearances affect the layout. Confirm delivery timing and inspect each appliance before installation because a late or substituted model can create cabinet and countertop changes.
